context_for_next_agent: CONTINUES 20260814-0542, which closed the migration/concurrency verification gap. This checkpoint covers the five-axis review that followed, which found a security issue larger than the diff under review. SECURITY, the headline: a PLAINTEXT PRODUCTION ADMIN PASSWORD was committed to this PUBLIC repo in .claude/PRPs/plans/completed/region-migration-frankfurt-phase1-2.plan.md — line 194 as ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD for the PROD seed step, and line 277 inside a curl login example that worked as-is. Readable by anyone since PR #65 (ed01955). It was ROTATED on Supabase and the rotation was VERIFIED by reading the stored hash back: new password accepted, old rejected. The new value lives ONLY in the untracked secrets/secret-keys.txt as JSK_PROD_ADMIN_PASSWORD — NEVER quote it in a tracked file, these handoff artifacts included. NO HISTORY REWRITE was performed: on a public repo the old value is permanently compromised, so rotation is the remedy and removing the lines (0c3c04a) only stops it being copied forward; `git log -S` still finds it in 5+ commits, which is expected. TWO GOTCHAS that both nearly produced a false success and must be repeated by anyone touching --target remote: (1) app/core/config.py:217 runs enforce_production_guards() at IMPORT time and backend/.env sets DEV_AUTH_BYPASS, so any script pointed at remote aborts with 'Unsafe production configuration' — pass DEV_AUTH_BYPASS=false, os.environ beats the dotenv file and this makes the run stricter not laxer; (2) settings.DATABASE_URL is a PostgresDsn, not a str, so calling .replace() on it raises AttributeError — str() it first. That second one silently killed the same safety check during the earlier local seed, and went unnoticed because the script had no `set -e`; what actually confirmed the local target was seed_admin's own printed header, not the assert. ALSO: seed_admin.py only updates a user literally named 'admin' — against any other name it prints 'Another admin user already exists, skipping' and rotates NOTHING while still exiting 0, so always confirm the account exists first. PROD holds exactly two ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN accounts: admin (id=1, active) and test_deactivated (id=4, ADMIN, is_active=False) — the latter is a leftover test account that should be deleted, deliberately not touched here as out of scope. THE REST OF THE TREE IS CLEAN: a full tracked-file scan found no API keys, JWTs, private keys or cloud credentials; every connection string with a password is a test fixture (user:secret, {canary}); and NO .env has ever been committed (`git log --all --diff-filter=A -- "*.env"` is empty, and .gitignore covers them). The one other password-shaped hit, admin1234, is unit-test fixture data in backend/tests/test_auth_login.py asserted to FAIL — not a credential, deliberately left alone. REVIEW FOLLOW-UPS applied in d31fbdf, all in the concurrency fixture: cleanup was deleting every booking with the test service type regardless of date and is now scoped to TARGET; the fixture yielded a tuple needing nested unpacking that discarded two names at one call site, and now yields a Race NamedTuple under the name `race`; teardown had no try/finally so a cleanup failure skipped engine.dispose() and leaked the pool. The negative control was RE-RUN after the refactor and still bites — removing pg_advisory_xact_lock fails the same two tests with two bookings sharing queue number 260817-001 — so the refactor did not weaken what they prove. ALSO ESTABLISHED: CI provides BOTH postgres:16 and redis:7 with DATABASE_URL matching the test default exactly (.github/workflows/ci.yml:70-93), which means the previous session's fixture fix was not polish — with Postgres present the skipif never applies, so the broken fixture would have produced 4 ERRORS on the very first push. TEST BASELINE unchanged: 870 passed / 0 failed / 60 errors, all 'Redis at 127.0.0.1:6379 not reachable', across 8 live-chat/websocket/auth files and no booking file. Warnings moved 4->5; all are pre-existing 'coroutine never awaited' from AsyncMock, none from booking. Nothing has been pushed.
